newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir rebels rally against India-Pakistan talks.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir rebels rally against India-Pakistan talks.

text.p: An umbrella group of Kashmiri separatist militants held a rally on Friday to protest against their exclusion from top-level talks between India and Pakistan.

Police said they had detained Shabir Ahmad Shah, a prominent separatist leader, and five others during the march by 100 supporters of the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference near the office of United Nations Military Observers Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP).

Top diplomats from India and Pakistan were due to meet in New Delhi on Friday for rare bilateral talks. No agenda has been announced for the discussions, but Pakistan insists that the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir is the "core issue".
The last round of talks in 1994 broke down over Kashmir, over which the neighbours have gone to war twice since 1947. India controls two-thirds of the region and Pakistan the rest.
The UNMOGIP was set up in 1949 to supervise a ceasefire between India and Pakistan in the territory.

The Hurriyat bands some 30 religious and political groups demanding a plebiscite in Kashmir that Pakistan, citing U.N. resolutions, has been campaigning for. India wants the dispute to be resolved bilaterally under a 1972 accord.

Shops were closed in Srinagar on Friday in response to a strike called by the Hurriyat. Most neighbourhoods in Srinagar, the summer capital of the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir, were deserted, except for security patrols.
"It is a historical tragedy that India and Pakistan did not involve the Kashmiris, the principal party, in the peace talks," a Hurriyat statement said.

"It is imperative to recall that the Kashmir issue is not a territorial dispute between India and Pakistan, but a matter of the social and political future and the lives of more than 12 million people," it said.
